new.headline: Ease back in after the fever. Walk Monday, then two short run-walks on Wednesday and Saturday, and don't try to make up the two runs you missed.

answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer:
No, don't add the two missed runs. Running hard to catch up is the most common way to turn a cold into a longer layoff, and a few days off costs you very little at this stage.

You will still have three sessions on your usual Monday, Wednesday and Saturday mornings. Only two are runs, and neither is longer than what you have already done. If the cough is clearly easing by next weekend, we go back to the planned build the week after.

new.analysis:
## What happened

Monday's walk-run went as planned, and you ran all eight 2-minute blocks. The cold and fever then took Wednesday and Saturday, and the rest days stayed rest days. Nothing was overrun, and nothing needs correcting except the idea of making up the missed runs.

## Why the step back

You had a fever of 38.4 on Wednesday night, and it has only been gone since Friday. You are still coughing, blocked up and wiped out. Your body is still recovering, so the first week back should ask for less than it can give. A gentle week costs you almost nothing. A relapse could cost you two or three more weeks.

## Where your fitness stands

You banked three consistent weeks before this, and the longest run grew each week. One week of missing sessions will not undo that. Eight weeks out from the race is still plenty of time for a beginner to build up to running the whole 5K.

## Effort on your easy runs

Your easy runs have sat at effort 6–7/10 and mostly in zone 3. That is a bit too hard for sessions meant to be easy, and it will be worse while you recover from illness, when heart rate runs higher for the same pace. Slowing the run blocks costs you nothing. Running the whole 5K is mostly about pacing, and slower pacing is what lets you keep running for longer.

## What comes next

There are no hard sessions for you yet, and that is deliberate. For a new runner, the build phase means more easy running time and slightly longer run blocks, not threshold work. If the next two runs feel fine, the following week returns to the planned build. That means 9 blocks of 2 minutes, then longer run blocks with shorter walks between them. If they don't feel fine, we repeat this week, which is a sensible choice.

Keep walking the dog as usual. Easy walks help you recover and don't count against the plan.

safetyCallouts.title: Get the cough checked if it lingers.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a fever of 38.4 and are still coughing and wiped out. If the fever returns, or you get chest pain, dizziness or breathlessness at rest, stop running and see a doctor. Do the same if the cough is not clearly better by next weekend. During a run, stop and walk home if your chest feels tight or you feel dizzy.
